thread:
sarah_pm: Quick sync — proposing a new "throughput window" add-on (per-route reserved throughput for short windows) to address customers hitting soft spikes. Need to agree on pricing shape, launch criteria, and contract language. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
ev an_product: Can you sketch the two pricing options? Fixed monthly vs credit-bucket? Which customers asked for this?
matt_revenue: Field asks came from 2 mid-market + 1 enterprise pilot. My leaning: commit + softcap. Sell a small reserved window (e.g., 1–4 hours/day) with guaranteed throughput; rollover credits for unused windows.
liz_sales: Buyers want something simple. They asked for predictable spend during marketing spikes. They hate per-request overage calculations. Rollover sounds attractive.
sarah_pm: Proposed shapes: (A) Monthly reserve SKU: X vCPU-equivalent throughput for N hours/day, fixed price. (B) Credit bucket: buy Y credits, consumed during peak, credits refill monthly, unused credits roll to next month for first 2 months.
ev an_product: Implementation note: runtime can enforce window caps, but per-route isolation + preferring cached responses during windows will be needed. Ops implications?
ops_bob: Runtime can support per-tenant windowing, but per-route isolation requires route-level routing table changes and a priority queue. Also need a fallback policy: when reserved window is exhausted, either fail fast or route to a cheaper model variant. Both are doable but not trivial. Estimate 3 sprints for infra + 1 sprint for rollout flags.
matt_revenue: Contract constraints: customers requested SLA during reserved windows. Legal will push back on hard uptime SLAs for these windows. We should offer a credit schedule (service credit for measurable missed throughput) rather than strict uptime SLAs.
legal_bot: Draft clause suggestion (for PM review): "During Purchased Throughput Windows, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet reserved throughput. If Redwood fails to meet reserved throughput for a calendar month, customer may claim service credits defined as X% of the monthly reservation fee per 1% below threshold, capped at Y%." Also: "No credits for force majeure or customer misconfiguration." Paste snippet into contract template and loop in Legal for exact numbers.
liz_sales: Field note: customers will accept credits but want a deterministic measurement window and visibility in console. Please add per-window telemetry and a CSV export for audits.
ev an_product: Agreed — console needs: per-window consumed vs reserved, peak latency percentiles, and automatic PDFable report for contracts. Also a feature flag to enable pilot customers only.
sarah_pm: Launch criteria proposal: 1) Runtime supports per-route reservation + fallback policy; 2) Console shows telemetry + CSV; 3) Legal-approved credit clause in contract; 4) Pilot with 3 named customers and acceptance tests; 5) Engineering smoke tests for revert/rollback.
matt_revenue: Pricing guardrails: start with high-margin pilot pricing (no discounts), measured usage during pilot. Post-pilot, we can standardize SKU and allow 10–15% introductory discount.
ops_bob: Implementation constraints: quantization/variant routing should be pluggable so fallback to cheaper model doesn't degrade semantics dangerously. We'll need a safety policy for hallucination-sensitive routes.
legal_bot: Also require customer to provide whitelisted IPs and a point-of-contact for escalation in contract.
sarah_pm: OK — action items: @evan_product write a one-pager comparing SKU vs credits and include telemetry fields. @ops_bob estimate infra tickets & timeline. @legal_bot produce contract language draft with suggested % caps. @liz_sales list 3 pilot customers and confirm willingness to sign pilot terms. I'll sync on Monday 9am. :calendar:
